0.name: zero
0.culture: Zero as a written number with its own value is credited to Indian mathematicians; in binary it is the 'off' state that half of all computing rests on.
0.commerce: Zeros make prices look round and premium (100, 1,000). Strings of zeros in phone numbers are easy to say but easy to mis-dial.

1.name: one
1.culture: One means first and unique in most cultures; in Indian gift-giving an extra 1 (101, 501, 1001) turns a round sum into a fresh start.
1.commerce: Ones read as 'first' and 'number one' — common in rankings, hotlines and brand names.

2.name: two
2.culture: In Chinese tradition good things come in pairs, so doubled digits (22, 88) are favoured for weddings and openings.
2.commerce: Pairs suggest bundles and two-for-one offers.

3.name: three
3.culture: Three signals completeness in Western storytelling and is considered lucky in Korean tradition; in Hinduism it echoes the trimurti.
3.commerce: The 'rule of three' drives good-better-best pricing tiers.

4.name: four
4.culture: In Chinese, Japanese and Korean, four sounds like the word for death, so many buildings skip fourth floors and buyers avoid 4s in phone numbers and plates.
4.commerce: Remove 4s from prices, plates, room numbers and phone numbers aimed at East Asian buyers — it is one of the strongest number effects in commerce.

5.name: five
5.culture: Five links to the five elements in Chinese philosophy and the five senses in the West.
5.commerce: Five-star ratings made 5 the universal symbol of quality.

6.name: six
6.culture: In Chinese, six sounds like 'smooth, flowing', and '666' is online slang for 'awesome'; in parts of the West, 666 carries negative religious associations.
6.commerce: Six-heavy numbers sell well to Chinese-speaking buyers; test before using 666 with Western audiences.

7.name: seven
7.culture: Seven is the West's classic lucky number — seven days, seven wonders, the 777 jackpot — and Japan has its Seven Lucky Gods. In Chinese it is mixed: the romantic Qixi festival, but also the seventh-month Ghost Month.
7.commerce: Seven-endings (27, 47, 97) are an internet-marketing habit; research favours 9-endings in general retail. Repeating sevens make memorable phone numbers and domains in Western markets.

8.name: eight
8.culture: In Chinese, eight (bā) sounds like 'prosper' (fā). The Beijing Olympics opened at 8 pm on 8/8/2008, and phone numbers and plates full of 8s sell at large premiums.
8.commerce: The single most valuable digit for Chinese-speaking buyers of prices, plates, phone numbers and numeric domains.

9.name: nine
9.culture: In Chinese, nine sounds like 'long-lasting', which makes it popular for weddings; in Japanese, ku can sound like 'suffering'.
9.commerce: Nine is the default retail price ending because of the left-digit effect (19.99 reads as 19).
